words.gloss: of the one with eight attributes

literal: Like sensory organs lacking perception, they have no quality indeed, the heads that do not bow to the feet of the one with eight attributes.
translation: The head that does not bow at the feet of the Lord of eight attributes is as useless as sensory organs that have lost their power of perception.
modern: எட்டுக் குணங்களை உடைய இறைவனுடைய திருவடிகளை வணங்காத மனிதர்களின் தலைகள், பார்க்கும் கேட்கும் தன்மைகள் இல்லாத கண் காது போன்ற ஐம்பொறிகளைப் போல எந்தப் பயனும் இல்லாதவை ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet compares a head that refuses to bow in humility before the Divine to sensory organs that have lost their ability to perceive. The term 'koḷ' refers to the act of receiving or perceiving sensory inputs, and 'poṟi' refers to the physical sense organs like eyes or ears. Just as an eye that cannot see or an ear that cannot hear is completely useless, a head that does not bow to the feet of the one with eight supreme attributes ('eṇkuṇattāṉ') lacks any real purpose or quality. The poet uses this vivid analogy to emphasize that humility and reverence are the essential functions of a conscious mind.
